about: CHAIN lindisfarne_book (Design/content/CHAINS.md; page Design/content/chains/lindisfarne_book.md; words Data/writing/chain_lindisfarne_book.json). A gospel book carried off from Lindisfarne on 8 June 793 and seen for sale in the north: found, bought, stolen or left, and what the bishop will do for the man who brings it home. Thirteen cards, from August 793 (the trail is open to 815; the island takes its book back in any year before 875). Part of the spine's threads holy_island and book_road: sets lf_trail_north, lf_knows_boys and lf_ransom_paid, bk_knows_worth, bk_parchment and bk_carried where a step is also the thread's step. Step flags ch_lindisfarne_book_1, _2, _3, _crew, _5, _6, _7, _8, _9; state flags _mount, _name, _marks, _words, _wrap, _aboard, _bought, _stolen, _seen, _caught, _retaken, _wet, _feud, _gift, _ransom, _shown, _alms, _left, _left_wait (a timer); endings ch_lindisfarne_book_end_home (history changed: changed_lindisfarne_book_home), ch_lindisfarne_book_end_york (history changed: changed_lindisfarne_book_york), ch_lindisfarne_book_end_alms (history changed: changed_lindisfarne_book_kings_gift), ch_lindisfarne_book_end_left (what the sources allow: nothing is recorded as coming back). The book is a flag (ch_lindisfarne_book_aboard), not a unit of the good 'books', so it cannot be sold by mistake at a market. The book itself is invented: a lesser gospel book of the house, not the great Gospels, which no early source says were harmed. Every option's note names its outcome text. Written 6 Oct 2026; a draft for the user to overwrite.

cards.note: Step 1, a start (drawn at Skiringssal, Ripa or Sliesthorp from August 793 to 803). A dealer in oddments has a strip of gilt bronze with knotwork and rivet holes: a mount torn from a book's board. Sources: church metalwork from Britain and Ireland cut up and worn as brooches is found in Norse women's graves of the ninth century (Wamers 1985, from memory) (?); the spine's holy_island hook at Skiringssal (a little house-shaped box, a cup, a strip of gilt): the house-shaped box is modelled on the shrine in Copenhagen with the later runes 'Ranvaik owns this casket' (from memory) (?). The dealer Ketil is invented (a common Norse name). Sets ch_lindisfarne_book_1 and the spine's lf_trail_north; buying sets ch_lindisfarne_book_mount; drinking sets ch_lindisfarne_book_name.

cards.title: A strip of gilt
cards.intention: On a dealer's cloth, between a cup and a little box shaped like a house, lies a strip of gilt bronze worked in knots, with four rivet holes and no rivets.

options.label: Buy the strip for twelve pennies' weight
options.note: outcome: chain_lindisfarne_book.s01.out_buy (the mount is a token: the bishop knows it at step 2)

options.label: Sit down with him over ale, in his own tongue

cards.note: Step 2, the other start (drawn at Lindisfarena while Higbald lives: to May 803). The bishop counts what is gone and tells how the book is known. Sources: Higbald, bishop 780 or 781 to 25 May 803 (Symeon, Historia Dunelmensis ecclesiae xx, tr. Stevenson 1855); Alcuin to Higbald, 793 (MGH Epistolae IV no. 20): he will speak to King Charles about the youths led away (not quoted); wine or ale allowed to the brethren since 737 (Symeon, Historia regum 854); the spine's hook (the names of the boys, the silver from the shrine, the cover of a gospel book; ransom in wax, wine or what silver is left). The book, its scribe Wigfrith (Wig- + -frith) and the hole in the first leaf of John are invented; scribes did write round holes in the skin. The great Gospels are said to be safe, which is all the sources allow. Cast: cast.higbald. Sets ch_lindisfarne_book_2, ch_lindisfarne_book_marks and the spine's lf_knows_boys.

cards.intention: The bishop stands in a church with its doors off and counts on his fingers what the heathen men took. He has done it before; he does not need to think.

cards.note: Step 3, optional (scheduled by step 2; the first call at Eoforwic after it). A scribe of the minster says what a book is worth and to whom. Sources: the great Gospels of Lindisfarne took some 150 calfskins (dossiers/lindisfarena.md); Alcuin's letter of 793 to King Aethelred (MGH Epistolae IV no. 16; texts_793.json alcuin_793), which the spine has read aloud at York; the spine's book_road hook (a scribe will price any book you describe: sets bk_knows_worth) and holy_island hook (the minster collecting for ransom); the riddle of the book (Exeter Book 26, Tupper 1910; riddles_793.json) tells the making of a gospel book from the calf to the gold. The Frisians' flight of 773 (Altfrid, Vita Liudgeri I.11) is the chain york_blood's; here it is one dry line. The scribe Eadwulf is invented (Ead- + -wulf). Sets ch_lindisfarne_book_3; learning sets bk_knows_worth; the order sets bk_parchment.

cards.note: Step 4, optional (a crew card, any time after step 1 or 2). The English lookout was schooled at Gyrwe and saw the book as a boy; his brother was an oblate on the island. Sources: the spine's cast (cast.crew.beornwine; his brother cast.tidwine) and its book_road hook for the crew (a wet book is a ruined book: where it rides in a seven-metre boat is a real question). Oiled or waxed skins as wrapping are ours (?). Sets ch_lindisfarne_book_crew; the wrap sets ch_lindisfarne_book_wrap; the lesson sets ch_lindisfarne_book_words and ch_lindisfarne_book_marks.

cards.title: The hole in the page
cards.intention: The English lookout has been quiet for a day, which is not like him. At the evening meal he says he has seen the book you are asking after.

cards.note: Step 5, the book itself (drawn at Ogvaldsnes or Skiringssal in the sailing months, from August 793 to 814, for anyone past step 1 or 2). The ship's chief who was west over the sea in 793 has it: the boards and the gold are gone, the leaves are whole, and he will sell for swords or weighed silver, never for prayers. Sources: the spine's hooks at Ogvaldsnes (a woman wears a brooch that was a book mount; he will sell for silver by weight or a sword, never for prayers; a book in a heathen house, the leaves kept because the pictures are fine); that Christians bought books back from the heathen with gold is the inscription of the Stockholm Codex Aureus, mid ninth century: the ealdorman Aelfred and his wife Werburg bought it from the heathen army with pure gold and gave it to Christ Church (our rendering, from memory) (?); no silver coin in the north, so the price is by weight (BRIEF.md rule 2). Who the raiders of 793 were is not known: Thorleif is the spine's invention. Cast: cast.thorleif; his wife Gunnhild is invented (Gunn- + -hildr). Sets ch_lindisfarne_book_5; buying sets _bought, _aboard and the spine's lf_ransom_paid; leaving it sets _seen; the night sets _stolen and _feud, or _caught.

cards.intention: A big red-fair man has a thing to show to anyone who trades with Christians: a block of sewn calfskins without boards, the first leaf a page of knots in red, yellow and green.

options.note: outcome: chain_lindisfarne_book.s05.out_silver

cards.note: Step 6 (at sea with the book aboard; drawn once). A sea is coming over the quarter and the book must ride somewhere. Sources: the spine's book_road hook for the crew; Symeon tells of a gospel book lost overboard about 880 and found unharmed on the sands (Historia Dunelmensis ecclesiae xxvi-xxvii): that is another book and a later story, and is not told here. Cast: cast.crew.aldger. Sets ch_lindisfarne_book_6; a failed chance sets ch_lindisfarne_book_wet (the book is spoiled in part, not lost).

options.note: outcome: chain_lindisfarne_book.s06.out_dry (sure; the wrap of step 4 pays here)

options.note: outcome: chain_lindisfarne_book.s06.out_drive_success / out_drive_failure (doubtful; the steersman says the worst first)

Sources: the spine's holy_island hook at sea (the same square sail seen again); the game has no battle screen, so this is a card (BRIEF.md). Cast: cast.thorleif, cast.crew.beornwine. options.label: Lie to and weigh out his price, with the price of his night's sleep on top
options.note: outcome: chain_lindisfarne_book.s07.out_pay (the feud ends; the book is yours by his own word)

options.label: Run for shoal water, where her keel cannot follow yours

options.label: Lie to and hand it back over the gunwale
options.note: outcome: chain_lindisfarne_book.s07.out_hand (costs pride only; he laughs, and the book is seen again at Sliesthorp)

memory.hand: handed the book back at sea

cards.note: Step 8, the second chance (scheduled at Sliesthorp 240 days after the book was left or the theft failed, 200 after it was retaken at sea: the next sailing year). The dealer in captives has the book in a lot, and a Svea is bidding for the skins. Sources: the spine's hooks at Sliesthorp (cast.asulf remembers every lot; Christians cannot be sold south to the Franks) and at Birka (cast.holmfast keeps an Englishman who can tally and read marks); skins scraped and written on again are known from every writing room; Asulf names prices in ounces of silver and never haggles twice (spine). Cast: cast.asulf, cast.holmfast. Sets ch_lindisfarne_book_8; buying sets _bought, _aboard and lf_ransom_paid; letting it go sets _left and the timer _left_wait (300 days).

cards.title: Asulf's lot
cards.intention: On a bench outside the dealer's pen, with a sealskin, two cups and a bell without a tongue, lies the block of calfskins. A spare, pale-eyed Svea is counting its leaves for the second time.

options.label: Outbid the Svea: fifteen ounces, two hundred and fifty pennies' weight
options.note: outcome: chain_lindisfarne_book.s08.out_silver

options.label: Give the dealer two Frankish swords for it
options.note: outcome: chain_lindisfarne_book.s08.out_blades (blades buy more captives than silver does, he says)

options.label: Tell the Svea truly what a house of monks would give for it, and let it go east
options.note: outcome: chain_lindisfarne_book.s08.out_tell (costs nothing; the Svea pays twenty ounces on your word, the book goes to Birka, and a year on the man who took it owes you for a true word)

memory.tell: told the book's true worth and let it go

cards.note: Step 9 (drawn at Lindisfarena with the book aboard, in any year before the community leaves in 875). The book is carried over the sand at low water. Sources: Higbald died 25 May 803; Ecgberht was consecrated at Bywell on 11 June 803 and was bishop to 821 (Symeon, Historia Dunelmensis ecclesiae xx; dossiers/lindisfarena.md); Cuthbert's day is 20 March and Aidan's 31 August (Bede, Historia ecclesiastica III.17); in Bede's day the house had no money, only cattle (HE III.26). Cast: cast.higbald, then the bishop of the year. Giving or ransoming sets ch_lindisfarne_book_9 with _gift or _ransom, clears _aboard and lf_ransom_paid and sets the spine's bk_carried; keeping it aboard sets _shown and the card may come again.

cards.note: ENDING home: history changed (drawn at Lindisfarena in March or August, the months of Cuthbert's and Aidan's days, after step 9). The book is laid on the altar and the house pays as it can. Sources: no source says that anything taken in 793 came back, so this is the player's doing; cloths that had lain on a saint's coffin were given as relics (the unlock table's unlock_relic_cuthbert_cloth); names of friends and givers were written in a book of life kept on the altar: Lindisfarne's own, the Durham Liber Vitae, is of about 840 and whether a list was kept in the 790s is not known (?); the king's men at Bebbanburg saw the sails and did not come (the spine's hook; not in any source) (?); by 854 the house held a dozen estates from the Tweed to the Tyne (Symeon, Historia regum 854). Cast: cast.higbald or the bishop of the year; the thegn Ecgwulf's kinsman is unnamed. Sets ch_lindisfarne_book_end_home and changed_lindisfarne_book_home; grand rewards unlock_title_cuthberts_man, unlock_relic_cuthbert_cloth (the giver's road only) or unlock_plot_lindisfarena.

cards.title: On the altar
cards.intention: On the feast the book lies open on the altar at the first leaf of John. The brethren from the estates are here, and a thegn from the king's rock, and a merchant who is asked to stand at the front.

options.label: Take what he offers the giver: your name in the book of life, a cloth from the saint's coffin, and the carrying of the house's wine
options.note: outcome: chain_lindisfarne_book.end_home.out_peace (the hard road's finale: 600 d that the thegn and York's collection press on you, two grand rewards and a commission)

options.label: Take the ransom: York's collection, the thegn's silver and the house's wax
options.note: outcome: chain_lindisfarne_book.end_home.out_silver (1,300 d in silver and wax, and the saint's peace)

options.label: Ask for ground instead: a boat strand and a storehouse inside the harbour sands
options.note: outcome: chain_lindisfarne_book.end_home.out_strand (640 d in silver and wax, and a plot on the bishop's island)

memory.peace: took the saint's peace and the cloth

cards.note: ENDING york: history changed (drawn at Eoforwic before 809 with the book aboard). The archbishop will buy it for the minster. Sources: Eanbald I died 10 August 796; Eanbald II, Alcuin's pupil, was archbishop from August 796 and is last heard of in 808; Alcuin scolded him for the armed men he kept (spine, cast.eanbald); the minster's library was the richest north of the Alps and is not heard of after the army took York in 866-867 (?); land in a town was a lord's to give: the unlock table has a house among the Frisians of York and a man there. Cast: cast.eanbald; the scribe Eadwulf, invented. Selling sets ch_lindisfarne_book_end_york, changed_lindisfarne_book_york and the lasting cost ch_lindisfarne_book_island_remembers; refusing costs his good opinion and the card may come again. Grand rewards unlock_factor_eoforwic or unlock_plot_eoforwic.

cards.note: ENDING alms: history changed (drawn at Quentovic from 794 to Alcuin's death in May 804, with the book aboard). Alcuin's letter-carrier waits at the hospice with his master's answer and the king's alms. Sources: Alcuin to Higbald, 793 (MGH Epistolae IV no. 20): when King Charles comes home he will go to him about the youths led away (not quoted); that the king gave alms for ransom is the spine's guess (?); Alcuin held the cell of Saint-Josse by Quentovic as a hospice for travellers from 792 (?); Gervold of Saint-Wandrille took the king's tolls at Quentovic to 806 (Gesta abbatum Fontanellensium c. 12); toll freedom at Quentovic was the king's to give, as to Saint-Germain in 779 (the unlock table's unlock_charter_quentovic); Alcuin was abbot of Tours from 796 and died 19 May 804. Cast: cast.sigewine, with cast.alcuin and cast.gervold spoken of. Giving it into his hands sets ch_lindisfarne_book_end_alms and changed_lindisfarne_book_kings_gift; taking the alms and carrying on sets ch_lindisfarne_book_alms (the turn). Grand reward unlock_charter_quentovic.

cards.note: ENDING left: what the sources allow (drawn at Ogvaldsnes or Skiringssal in the sailing months, 300 days or more after the book was let go at step 8). Nothing taken in 793 is recorded as coming home; the mounts are worn as brooches and the leaves are at Birka. The man who took it owes for a true word. Sources: as step 1 for the brooches; walrus ivory came south from the far north of Norway (Ohthere's account to King Alfred, about 890; texts_793.json ohthere); the Karmsund is the sheltered way north that Ogvaldsnes stands on (ports_793.json); guest-friendship and laying goods together (felag: the unlock table's unlock_partner_felagi; the word is on rune stones of the tenth century and later, so for the 790s it is an older custom under a later name) (?); the spine's Birka hook (a Svea keeps an Englishman who can read marks: cast.tidwine, who is the chain holy_island's to find). Cast: cast.thorleif; Gunnhild, invented. Sets ch_lindisfarne_book_end_left; grand rewards unlock_title_thorleifs_guest, unlock_partner_felagi (with the lasting cost ch_lindisfarne_book_raiders_friend) or unlock_pilot_karmsund (with ch_lindisfarne_book_word, word carried to the island).

cards.title: A true word
cards.intention: The big red-fair man sees your sail before you see him, and sends a boy down to say there is a place for you on the bench and that nobody will ask what you paid for it.

options.label: Take his gift of walrus tooth, and a guest's place in his hall and on his coast
options.note: outcome: chain_lindisfarne_book.end_left.out_tusks (eight tusks, about 720 d, and a chief's guest-right)

options.label: Lay goods together with his sister's son, who has a boat and no silver
options.note: outcome: chain_lindisfarne_book.end_left.out_felag (five bundles of marten, about 600 d, and a sworn partner; Christians will hear whose kin he is)

options.label: Take your share by weight and the marks of the sound, and carry word to the island of where its book lies
options.note: outcome: chain_lindisfarne_book.end_left.out_word (600 d, the Karmsund's marks, and a thing to tell the bishop)

memory.tusks: took a guest's place in the hall
memory.felag: laid goods together with his kinsman
memory.word: took his share and the marks of the sound
